# Requirements

Requirement IDs are permanent. Do not reuse or renumber an ID; supersede it by
linking a replacement requirement. Each requirement must be provable by a
command, a GitHub record, or an observable behavior.

| REQ-045 | GitHub and Git remain the durable work plane. | REQ-046 | One Task has one Task supervisor and one authoritative Plan; each writing PR has exactly one active PR worker, isolated worktree, branch, writer lease, and disjoint ownership boundary. Until the REQ-053 activation gate is replaced by a later human agreement, a Task has at most one writing PR; released replacement workers may act sequentially on that same PR. A supervisor never writes while a worker is active, and no two active workers may write the same PR, worktree, branch, or ownership boundary. | Current source two-tier model; ADR-0005 | Lifecycle fixtures and a live trial prove PR-to-worker cardinality, worktree/branch isolation, supervisor non-writing behavior, disjoint ownership, release-before-replacement, and rejection of a second active writer. | accepted |
| REQ-047 | Every writing worker is preceded by an immutable post-Plan dispatch record and every replacement by a proven stop/fence plus immutable release. The records bind Task/Plan, explicit provider, surface/versioned runtime reference, monotonically increasing attempt, durable supervisor and worker references, repository, PR, exact branch/base, stable worktree identity, ownership, lease, predecessor, verification, and stop conditions without personal paths or credentials. Uncertain termination pauses for human adjudication rather than expiring ownership by time or thread disappearance. | Current source dispatch/release ritual; ADR-0005 | Deterministic chronology/complete-identity/replacement fixtures plus crash/recovery Task #76 and a fresh-session stale-writer negative trial. | accepted |
| REQ-048 | A Task supervisor may implement without a separate PR worker only when its authoritative Plan, posted before every Task commit, contains the exact declaration `no worker will be spawned` and justifies one PR/one writer. The rows say `accepted` because the agreement merge enacts this document. While
the pull request remains open, the diff is only a proposal. A later change
supersedes requirements through a new agreement merge; it does not silently
rewrite their meaning.
